examples.zh: 我在健身日志里看到 rep，问它是不是指「一次重复动作」。

examples.en: The instructor wrote rep on the board and explained how people use the term.
examples.zh: 教练在白板上写了 rep，解释日志里每「一次重复动作」怎么记。

words.enDefinition: a fan version of the shirt worn by a team's players

examples.en: My roommate wore a replica jersey over two sweaters at the match.
examples.zh: 室友那场比赛穿了两件毛衣，外面套了件「球迷版队服」。

examples.en: I recognised my cousin by the bright blue replica jersey she wore.
examples.zh: 我凭表姐那件亮蓝色的「球迷版队服」认出了她。

words.enDefinition: To tell staff when shared exercise equipment is damaged or visibly unsafe to use.

examples.en: The staff showed our orientation group where to report damaged equipment after the tour.
examples.zh: 参观结束后，工作人员告诉我们新生小组到哪里「报告器械损坏」。

examples.en: The notice beside the desk asked visitors to report damaged equipment to the attendant.
examples.zh: 服务台旁的告示请来访者向值班员「报告器械损坏」。

collocations: ask visitors to report damaged equipment
a reminder to report damaged equipment
show where to report damaged equipment

words.enDefinition: to roll the same die or dice again

examples.en: The rule allowed me to reroll if the dice landed off the mat.
examples.zh: 规则允许骰子掉到垫子外面时「重新掷骰子」。

examples.en: My friend decided to reroll after reading the optional rule on the card.
examples.zh: 朋友看了牌上的可选规则后，决定「重新掷骰子」。

words.enDefinition: A later broadcast of a television program that has already been shown.

examples.en: I caught a rerun of the interview while waiting for my laundry to finish.
examples.zh: 等衣服洗好时，我碰巧看到那次访谈的「重播」。

examples.en: The schedule showed a rerun at noon for anyone who missed the evening program.
examples.zh: 节目表上写着中午有「重播」，方便没看晚间节目的人补看。

collocations: a rerun of an old show

words.enDefinition: a secondary team within a sports club, often featuring developing or backup players

examples.en: She played for the reserve team during her first year at the university.
examples.zh: 她大学第一年在「预备队」效力。

examples.en: The reserve team had an early fixture before the main squad arrived that afternoon.
examples.zh: 首队当天下午来到之前，「预备队」有场更早的比赛。

words.enDefinition: A long elastic strip or loop that provides resistance as it stretches during exercise.

examples.en: I spotted a resistance band hanging from a hook beside the storage shelves today.
examples.zh: 我今天看到储物架旁的一个挂钩上挂着一条「弹力训练带」。

examples.en: The studio had a box marked resistance band beside a smaller box for clips.
examples.zh: 团课教室有个标着「弹力训练带」的箱子，旁边的小盒子放夹子。

words.enDefinition: a supply of tokens or materials available during the game

examples.en: I returned the extra green tokens to the shared resource pool.
examples.zh: 我把多出的绿色标记物放回共享的「游戏资源池」。

examples.en: The resource pool ran low near the end of our second round.
examples.zh: 第二轮快结束时，「游戏资源池」里的资源不多了。

collocations: return something to the resource pool

words.enDefinition: A day intentionally set aside from a usual exercise routine.

examples.en: My roommate marked a rest day in the calendar before making plans for the weekend.
examples.zh: 室友在安排周末活动前，在日历上标了一天「不安排锻炼的休息日」。

examples.en: I noted a rest day in my log when I spent Saturday at the library.
examples.zh: 星期六一整天都在图书馆，我在日志里记了个「不安排锻炼的休息日」。

collocations: mark a rest day in a log

words.enDefinition: A period of rest between parts of an exercise session.

examples.en: Our sample log had a space for the rest interval between two exercise entries.
examples.zh: 示例日志里，两条练习记录之间留了一栏填写「运动间歇」。

examples.en: The instructor answered my question about a class change during the rest interval that afternoon.
examples.zh: 当天下午，教练在「运动间歇」回答了我关于课程变动的问题。

words.enDefinition: to begin the current stage again from its start

examples.en: I asked if we could restart the level after missing the first clue.
examples.zh: 漏掉第一条线索后，我问能不能「重新开始当前关卡」。

examples.en: My friend chose to restart the level to try the quicker route.
examples.zh: 朋友选择「重新开始当前关卡」，试试更快的路线。

collocations: restart the level from the menu

words.enDefinition: a display summarising how players performed after a game or round

examples.en: The results screen showed how many shapes each pair had matched.
examples.zh: 「结果页面」显示各组分别配对了多少个图形。

examples.en: We waited for the results screen before deciding whether to play again.
examples.zh: 我们等「结果页面」显示后，再决定要不要再玩一局。

words.enDefinition: a menu option to continue playing after a pause

examples.en: I chose “Resume game” after helping my roommate find a spare controller.
examples.zh: 帮室友找到备用手柄后，我选择了「继续游戏」。

examples.en: The “Resume game” button took me back to the middle of the level.
examples.zh: 「继续游戏」按钮把我带回了关卡中途。

words.enDefinition: To start a paused or stopped video again from the position already reached.

examples.en: I pressed the button to resume playback after my roommate came back with tea.
examples.zh: 室友拿着茶回来后，我按了按钮「恢复播放」。

examples.en: Could you resume playback now that everyone is back from the kitchen with snacks?
examples.zh: 大家已经从厨房拿完零食回来了，你能「恢复播放」吗？

words.enDefinition: a game that asks players to perform actions in time with music

examples.en: We played a rhythm game by tapping along to a gentle song.
examples.zh: 我们跟着一首轻柔的歌打拍子，玩了会儿「音游」。

examples.en: My roommate tried the rhythm game with the volume turned down.
examples.zh: 室友把音量调低，试了一下那个「音游」。

words.enDefinition: a guitarist who mainly plays chords or rhythmic parts to support a song

examples.en: The rhythm guitarist kept playing quietly while the singer spoke to the audience.
examples.zh: 歌手和观众说话时，「节奏吉他手」继续轻声伴奏。

examples.en: Our rhythm guitarist suggested a slower pattern when we rehearsed the second number.
examples.zh: 排练第二首歌时，我们的「节奏吉他手」建议把节奏型放慢。

words.enDefinition: a very loud sound made by many spectators at once

examples.en: I could hear the roar of the crowd from outside the arena doors.
examples.zh: 站在体育馆门外也能听到「观众席的欢呼声」。

examples.en: It was hard to speak over the roar of the crowd after that moment.
examples.zh: 那一刻过后，「观众席的欢呼声」大得让人很难听清说话。

collocations: hear the roar of the crowd
over the roar of the crowd
drowned out by the roar of the crowd

words.enDefinition: to throw dice so they land on randomly selected faces

examples.en: The game asked us to roll the dice after choosing a colour.
examples.zh: 游戏要求我们选好颜色后「掷骰子」。

examples.en: I waited to roll the dice until my classmate had moved her counter.
examples.zh: 我等同学移好标记物才「掷骰子」。

collocations: take turns to roll the dice
roll the dice at the start of a turn
be the first to roll the dice

words.enDefinition: A humorous film or show about people falling in love or navigating a relationship.

examples.en: We felt like watching a romantic comedy after spending the afternoon finishing our final projects.
examples.zh: 下午把期末项目做完后，我们想看一部「浪漫喜剧」。

examples.en: The romantic comedy was funnier when it showed the couple making ordinary mistakes together.
examples.zh: 这部「浪漫喜剧」里，两人一起犯日常小错误的片段更好笑。

words.enDefinition: the order in which volleyball players change positions around the court

examples.en: The referee checked our rotation order before allowing the next serve to go ahead.
examples.zh: 裁判查了我们的「排球轮转顺序」，才允许下一球发出。

examples.en: Our coach explained the rotation order before everyone went back out on the court.
examples.zh: 所有人回到场上之前，教练解释了「排球轮转顺序」。

words.enDefinition: a temporary mix made to hear how the recorded elements fit together

examples.en: The tutor listened to our rough mix before suggesting changes to the guitar level.
examples.zh: 导师听了我们的「初步混音」后，建议改动吉他的音量。

examples.en: I saved the rough mix so we could compare it with the final version.
examples.zh: 我保存了「初步混音」，方便和最终版比较。

collocations: listen back to the rough mix

words.enDefinition: a quick drawing that shows a basic idea without finished detail

examples.en: I made a rough sketch of the room before drawing any faces.
examples.zh: 画人物的脸之前，我先给房间画了张「草图」。

examples.en: My classmate showed me a rough sketch during our short break.
examples.zh: 短暂休息时，同学给我看了一张「草图」。

words.enDefinition: a competition format in which every participant or team plays every other in a group

examples.en: The club used a round robin so everyone could play more than one match.
examples.zh: 俱乐部采用「循环赛」，这样每个人都能打不止一场。

examples.en: We consulted the round robin schedule before booking the courts for Saturday morning.
examples.zh: 订周六上午的球场之前，我们看了「循环赛」的赛程。

words.enDefinition: a letter showing which row a particular seat is in

examples.en: I read the row letter twice because it looked like a number.
examples.zh: 那个「排号字母」看起来像数字，所以我看了两遍。

examples.en: The row letter was on the sign at the end of the aisle.
examples.zh: 过道尽头的牌子上写着「排号字母」。

words.enDefinition: a sign or label identifying a row of seats

examples.en: The row marker was hard to read from the bottom of the steps.
examples.zh: 站在台阶下，很难看清「座位排号标识」。

examples.en: We checked the row marker before asking the usher to help us.
examples.zh: 我们先核对了「座位排号标识」，再请引座员帮忙。

words.enDefinition: A stationary exercise machine that imitates much of the movement of rowing a boat.

examples.en: The rowing machine was by the entrance, just across from the shelf for towels.
examples.zh: 「划船机」在入口旁，正对着放毛巾的架子。

examples.en: My classmate drew a rowing machine on the map so our group could recognize it.
examples.zh: 同学在地图上画了一台「划船机」，方便小组其他人认出来。

words.enDefinition: a guideline placing subjects near thirds of the image rather than the centre

examples.en: I tried the rule of thirds while photographing the quiet lake.
examples.zh: 拍那片平静的湖时，我试了试「三分构图法」。

examples.en: The camera grid helped me remember the rule of thirds during the walk.
examples.zh: 散步拍照时，相机网格线提醒我使用「三分构图法」。

words.enDefinition: a booklet explaining how to set up and play a game

examples.en: We checked the rulebook after both of us wanted to move first.
examples.zh: 我们两人都想先走，就查了查「游戏规则手册」。

examples.en: The rulebook had an example of a complete turn on the last page.
examples.zh: 「游戏规则手册」最后一页举了一个完整回合的例子。

words.enDefinition: a rehearsal in which performers go through a piece or a substantial section from start to finish

examples.en: We finished the first run-through just before the rehearsal room closed.
examples.zh: 排练室快关门时，我们刚完成第一次「完整走排」。

examples.en: The director watched the run-through without stopping to give notes.
examples.zh: 导演看完了「完整走排」，没有叫停来提意见。

words.enDefinition: The total amount of time a film or episode runs from start to finish.

examples.en: I checked the runtime because our class needed time for discussion after the documentary.
examples.zh: 我们班看完纪录片还要留时间讨论，所以我查了「片长」。

examples.en: The runtime was listed below the synopsis in the program for the campus screening.
examples.zh: 校园放映的节目单在内容简介下面列了「片长」。

words.enDefinition: A clip that forms part of the emergency stop system on some treadmills.

examples.en: The orientation handout showed a safety clip beside a drawing of the treadmill display.
examples.zh: 入门介绍资料在跑步机屏幕的示意图旁画了一个「跑步机安全夹」。

examples.en: A student asked what the safety clip was while our group looked at the machine.
examples.zh: 我们小组看器械时，一名同学问什么是「跑步机安全夹」。

collocations: a safety clip on a treadmill
a diagram showing the safety clip
the label beside the safety clip

words.enDefinition: an option for building or experimenting without a fixed objective

examples.en: Our group used sandbox mode to plan a little model town together.
examples.zh: 我们小组用「沙盒模式」一起布置一个小镇模型。

examples.en: My friend likes sandbox mode because she can design whatever she wants.
examples.zh: 朋友喜欢「沙盒模式」，因为想设计什么都可以。

words.enDefinition: to store your current progress before closing or leaving a game

examples.en: We chose to save and quit when the library started to close.
examples.zh: 图书馆开始清场时，我们选择了「保存后退出」。

examples.en: The game asked whether to save and quit before returning to the menu.
examples.zh: 回到菜单前，游戏询问是否「保存后退出」。

words.enDefinition: one place in a list for storing a saved game

examples.en: I chose a new save slot so I wouldn't overwrite my friend's progress.
examples.zh: 我选了新的「存档槽位」，这样就不会覆盖朋友的游戏进度。

examples.en: The game showed the date next to each save slot on screen.
examples.zh: 游戏在屏幕上每个「存档槽位」旁显示保存日期。

words.enDefinition: to read a ticket with a device to check it

examples.en: The volunteer pointed to the reader and said, "Please scan your ticket here."
examples.zh: 志愿者指着扫码器说：「请在这里扫描你的门票」。

examples.en: The sign reminded everyone to scan your ticket before going through the gate.
examples.zh: 告示提醒大家过闸口前「扫描自己的门票」。

collocations: ask someone to scan your ticket
scan your ticket at the gate

words.enDefinition: a transition when the performance moves to a new stage setting

examples.en: The piano played during the scene change while the actors moved offstage.
examples.zh: 演员离开舞台时，钢琴在「换景」期间演奏。

examples.en: The scene change only took a moment because we moved one table.
examples.zh: 我们只挪了一张桌子，所以很快就完成了「换景」。

words.enDefinition: A performer who attracts the most attention in a scene, even in a smaller part.

examples.en: The actor playing the quiet neighbor turned out to be the scene-stealer of the film.
examples.zh: 演安静邻居的演员成了片中最「抢戏的演员」。

examples.en: One reviewer called the young actor a scene-stealer after watching the library scene twice.
examples.zh: 一位影评人看了两遍图书馆那场戏后，称这位年轻演员是「抢戏的演员」。

words.enDefinition: a painted or printed background used behind performers on stage

examples.en: Our scenic backdrop showed the university town in summer from across the river.
examples.zh: 我们的「舞台背景幕」上画的是从河对岸看去的夏日大学城。

examples.en: I helped paint the trees on the scenic backdrop after afternoon class.
examples.zh: 下午下课后，我帮忙在「舞台背景幕」上画树。

words.enDefinition: Fiction that imagines developments in science, technology, or the worlds they might shape.

examples.en: I usually watch science fiction for the ideas about technology rather than the space settings.
examples.zh: 我看「科幻题材」作品，通常更关注里面对技术的想象。

examples.en: The science fiction series imagined a future where people could share memories with friends.
examples.zh: 这部「科幻题材」剧集想象在未来人们能和朋友分享记忆。

words.enDefinition: a sheet used to write down points during or after play

examples.en: I added my total to the score sheet for the final round.
examples.zh: 我把自己的总分填在最后一轮的「计分表」上。

examples.en: My friend checked the score sheet before we packed up the game.
examples.zh: 收游戏之前，朋友核对了「计分表」。

words.enDefinition: a printed path where a marker shows a running score

examples.en: The score track ran around the edge of the board beside the cards.
examples.zh: 「计分轨」沿着棋盘边缘一圈，挨着那些牌。

examples.en: I moved my marker along the score track after finishing the set.
examples.zh: 集齐一套后，我把标记沿「计分轨」往前移了。

collocations: a score track on the board

words.enDefinition: a display showing the current score at a sports event

examples.en: The scoreboard was hard to read from the upper seating section.
examples.zh: 从上层座席很难看清「现场记分牌」。

examples.en: We looked at the scoreboard before heading back to our seats.
examples.zh: 回座位前，我们看了一眼「现场记分牌」。

words.enDefinition: collecting and arranging photographs, keepsakes and words in a book

examples.en: My roommate started scrapbooking to record her first term at university.
examples.zh: 为了记录大学第一个学期，室友开始「制作剪贴簿」。

examples.en: I tried scrapbooking with bus tickets and notes from friends that weekend.
examples.zh: 那个周末，我试着用公交票和朋友的便条「制作剪贴簿」。

words.enDefinition: The number identifying the room where a film is being shown in a cinema.

examples.en: I checked the screen number before asking which corridor led to our auditorium.
examples.zh: 我先核对了「影厅编号」，然后问走哪条走廊能到我们那一厅。

examples.en: The screen number on the digital ticket matched the sign beside the correct door.
examples.zh: 电子票上的「影厅编号」和对应门旁的标牌一致。

collocations: the screen number on the ticket

words.enDefinition: A room set up to show films or other recorded video to an audience.

examples.en: We found the screening room just beyond the exhibition space in the arts building.
examples.zh: 我们在艺术楼的展览区过去一点找到了「放映厅」。

examples.en: The screening room was big enough for our class but much smaller than a regular cinema.
examples.zh: 「放映厅」够我们全班坐，不过比普通影院小得多。

words.enDefinition: The final episode in a season of a television series.

examples.en: The season finale answered one question but left us guessing what would happen next.
examples.zh: 「一季的最后一集」解答了一个疑问，却又让我们猜接下来会发生什么。

examples.en: We saved the season finale for Friday because nobody could stay up late that night.
examples.zh: 那晚谁都不能熬夜，我们就把「一季的最后一集」留到星期五再看。

collocations: a surprise in the season finale

words.enDefinition: The first episode of a particular season of a television series.

examples.en: The season opener introduced a new classmate before returning to the story from last year.
examples.zh: 「新一季首集」先介绍了一位新同学，才接着讲去年的情节。

examples.en: My flatmates saved the season opener to watch together when everyone returned from break.
examples.zh: 室友们把「新一季首集」留着，等大家放假回来再一起看。

words.enDefinition: someone who has a pass for a set of seasonal games

examples.en: My neighbour is a season-ticket holder and knows everyone in her row.
examples.zh: 邻居是「赛季通票持有人」，认识她那一排的所有人。

examples.en: A season-ticket holder showed me the fastest route to the upper seats.
examples.zh: 一位「赛季通票持有人」给我指了去上层座位最近的路。

words.enDefinition: indicates that selected seats are no longer kept for the buyer

examples.en: The website showed "Seat hold expired", so the selected seats went back on sale.
examples.zh: 网站显示「座位暂留已超时」，选中的座位重新开放出售。

examples.en: I saw "Seat hold expired" after a long phone call interrupted my booking.
examples.zh: 一个长电话打断了订票过程，挂断后我看到了「座位暂留已超时」。

words.enDefinition: a named or numbered group of seats within a venue

examples.en: The staff member pointed us toward the right seating section upstairs.
examples.zh: 工作人员指给我们楼上的正确「观众席分区」。

examples.en: The map used different colours for each seating section around the court.
examples.zh: 场馆地图用不同颜色标出球场周围的每个「观众席分区」。

words.enDefinition: seats positioned beyond the goal at one end of the field

examples.en: Our seats behind the goal gave us a clear view of the players celebrating.
examples.zh: 坐在「球门后方座位」上，我们能清楚看到球员庆祝。

examples.en: My cousin chose seats behind the goal because she preferred that end of the stadium.
examples.zh: 表姐喜欢体育场那一端，所以选了「球门后方座位」。

collocations: watch from seats behind the goal

words.enDefinition: the additional serve permitted when the first one at a tennis point is a fault

examples.en: I watched the second serve land near the line after her first went long.
examples.zh: 她一发出界后，我看见「第二发球」落在界线附近。

examples.en: My doubles partner paused before her second serve while someone retrieved the first ball.
examples.zh: 有人去捡一发的球，我的双打搭档等了一下才发「第二发球」。

words.enDefinition: a gathering where people exchange seeds for gardens or pots

examples.en: I brought two labelled envelopes to the neighbourhood seed swap.
examples.zh: 我带了两个贴好标签的信封去参加社区「种子交换活动」。

examples.en: The library hosted a seed swap at the start of spring.
examples.zh: 初春，图书馆办了一次「种子交换活动」。

words.enDefinition: a shallow divided container for starting seeds

examples.en: I labelled each part of the seed tray with a pencil.
examples.zh: 我用铅笔给「育苗盘」的每一格做了标记。

examples.en: The seed tray sat in the sunny corner beside our window.
examples.zh: 「育苗盘」放在我们窗边有阳光的角落。

words.enDefinition: a team given a tournament position based on its ranking or previous results

examples.en: Our group was drawn against a seeded team in the first match on Saturday.
examples.zh: 我们组周六的第一场比赛抽到了一支「种子队」。

examples.en: The seeded team had finished near the top of the league the previous year.
examples.zh: 那支「种子队」前一年在联赛里名列前茅。

words.enDefinition: to choose which stage of a game to play

examples.en: I asked my friend to select a level we could finish quickly.
examples.zh: 我请朋友「选一个我们能很快通关的关卡」。

examples.en: The menu let us select a level by its number or name.
examples.zh: 菜单让我们可以按编号或名称「选择关卡」。

collocations: select a level from the menu
ask players to select a level

words.enDefinition: A pin on some gym machines that determines which weights are engaged.

examples.en: The attendant pointed to the selector pin on a diagram beside the exercise machine.
examples.zh: 值班员指给我们看器械旁的图上哪一处是「配重选择销」。

examples.en: My classmate recognized the selector pin from a picture in the gym orientation guide.
examples.zh: 同学根据健身房入门手册的图片认出了「配重选择销」。

collocations: a diagram of the selector pin
a label for the selector pin

words.enDefinition: a camera feature that delays taking a picture after activation

examples.en: I used the self-timer so I could join my friends in the photo.
examples.zh: 我用了「延时自拍功能」，这样就能和朋友一起入镜。

examples.en: The self-timer beeped while we stood in front of the display.
examples.zh: 我们站在展板前时，「延时自拍功能」发出了提示音。

collocations: take a photo with the self-timer

words.enDefinition: an audience at an event for which all tickets were sold

examples.en: The final drew a sellout crowd even though it was a weekday.
examples.zh: 虽然是工作日，决赛还是吸引了「满座的观众」。

examples.en: I had never heard a sellout crowd cheer inside such a small arena.
examples.zh: 我从没在这么小的体育馆里听过「满座的观众」一起欢呼。

words.enDefinition: a contest that determines which participant or team goes through to the final

examples.en: We watched the semifinal from the side of the court after our game finished.
examples.zh: 自己的比赛打完后，我们在场边看了「半决赛」。

examples.en: My roommate had a class at the same time as the semifinal that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，我室友上课正好和「半决赛」撞时间。

words.enDefinition: The last episode of an entire television show, in North American usage.

examples.en: We watched the series finale together after following the show since our first year.
examples.zh: 我们从大一开始追这部剧，最后一起看了「整部剧的最终集」。

examples.en: The series finale showed where several of the characters ended up after leaving town.
examples.zh: 「整部剧的最终集」讲了几位角色离开小镇后各有怎样的去向。

words.enDefinition: a volleyball serve that directly scores a point

examples.en: The team celebrated a service ace at the start of the volleyball set.
examples.zh: 排球这局刚开始，队员就为一次「发球直接得分」庆祝。

examples.en: Our player delivered a service ace after the returner moved farther to the left.
examples.zh: 接球人往左移动一些之后，我们的队员「发球直接得分」。

words.enDefinition: one of the marked areas into which a legal tennis serve must land

examples.en: His first serve landed in the service box close to the centre line.
examples.zh: 他的一发落在「发球区」内，靠近中线。

examples.en: I checked the lines of the service box before we began our practice match.
examples.zh: 练习赛开始前，我核对了「发球区」的界线。

words.enDefinition: a musician hired to play for a recording or particular performance

examples.en: A session musician played the piano parts on my friend's first recording at college.
examples.zh: 我朋友在学院第一次录音时，一名「受聘乐手」弹了钢琴声部。

examples.en: Our tutor had worked as a session musician before coming back to teach.
examples.zh: 导师回来教书前做过「受聘乐手」。

words.enDefinition: a mechanism where players gather matching or related items to earn points

examples.en: We learned how set collection worked by grouping the cards by symbol.
examples.zh: 我们按图案把牌分组，弄明白了「集套得分机制」怎么玩。

examples.en: The rules gave an example of set collection on the final page.
examples.zh: 规则最后一页举了个「集套得分机制」的例子。

collocations: a game based on set collection

words.enDefinition: the person who designs the physical scenery for a production

examples.en: The set designer drew a flat with very little furniture for our play.
examples.zh: 「舞台布景设计师」为我们的剧画了一套没几件家具的公寓。

examples.en: Our set designer gave the library scene a wall of painted books.
examples.zh: 我们的「舞台布景设计师」为图书馆那场戏画了一墙的书。

words.enDefinition: the first piece of music in a performer’s set

examples.en: They chose a fast set opener to get the audience moving before the slower songs.
examples.zh: 他们选了一首快歌作「一轮演出的开场曲」，好在慢歌之前让观众动起来。

examples.en: I recognised the set opener from a recording our tutor played in class.
examples.zh: 我从导师课上放过的一段录音里认出了「一轮演出的开场曲」。

words.enDefinition: a point that can end the current set if the player or team ahead wins it

examples.en: Our pair saved a set point before winning the next two rallies in doubles.
examples.zh: 双打中，我们这对组合先挽救了一个「盘点」，随后赢了接下来的两个回合。

examples.en: The player took a breath before serving on set point in the first set.
examples.zh: 第一盘打到「盘点」时，球员发球前深吸了一口气。

words.enDefinition: to arrange the board and its starting pieces before playing

examples.en: My roommate helped me set up the board before the others arrived.
examples.zh: 其他人来之前，室友帮我「摆好了棋盘」。

examples.en: We took two minutes to set up the board for the new game.
examples.zh: 我们花了两分钟给新游戏「摆好棋盘」。

collocations: help someone set up the board
set up the board before playing
be ready to set up the board

words.enDefinition: the list of pieces a performer plans to play in a particular order

examples.en: The setlist was taped to the floor beside the guitarist's shoes during the show.
examples.zh: 演出时，「演出曲目单」贴在吉他手脚边的地板上。

examples.en: I checked the setlist after the gig to find the name of the last song.
examples.zh: 演出结束后，我查了「演出曲目单」，想找最后一首歌的名字。

words.enDefinition: the volleyball player who usually delivers the ball to a hitter

examples.en: Our setter moved closer to the net as the ball came across the court.
examples.zh: 球从场地另一侧过来时，我们的「排球二传手」移到更靠近球网的地方。

examples.en: The coach introduced the new setter before we started the afternoon practice.
examples.zh: 下午训练开始前，教练介绍了新来的「排球二传手」。

words.enDefinition: a picture showing where pieces go before play begins

examples.en: We used the setup diagram to put the starting pieces in place.
examples.zh: 我们按照「游戏摆放示意图」摆好了起始棋子。

examples.en: The setup diagram was clearer than the long paragraph in the booklet.
examples.zh: 「游戏摆放示意图」比小册子里那段长说明更清楚。

words.enDefinition: a small collection of items for sewing or mending

examples.en: The flat had a sewing kit in the drawer beside the table.
examples.zh: 合租公寓的桌边抽屉里有个「针线包」。

examples.en: I brought a sewing kit for the little patch we were making.
examples.zh: 我们要做一小块布贴，我就带了个「针线包」。

words.enDefinition: a place sheltered from direct sunlight

examples.en: We found a shaded spot for lunch beside the old tree.
examples.zh: 我们在老树旁找了个「背阴处」吃午饭。

examples.en: I moved my sketchbook to a shaded spot when my seat got sunny.
examples.zh: 原来坐的地方晒到太阳后，我把速写本挪到「背阴处」。

words.enDefinition: the use of light and dark areas to suggest shape

examples.en: The shading made my pencil drawing look rounder than I expected.
examples.zh: 「明暗处理」让我的铅笔画看起来比预想的更有立体感。

examples.en: I asked my classmate to explain the shading on the side of the cup.
examples.zh: 我请同学解释杯子侧面的「明暗处理」。

words.enDefinition: printed or digital notation showing how a piece should be played or sung

examples.en: I left the sheet music on the piano after working through the second page.
examples.zh: 练完第二页后，我把「乐谱」留在钢琴上。

examples.en: My tutor emailed the sheet music before we chose a time for our first rehearsal.
examples.zh: 我们选定第一次排练的时间之前，导师发来了「乐谱」。

words.enDefinition: protective pieces worn over the front of the lower legs in sports

examples.en: I packed my shin guards in the side pocket before leaving for the match.
examples.zh: 出发去比赛前，我把「护腿板」放进了侧袋。

examples.en: The captain brought spare shin guards for players who had forgotten their own.
examples.zh: 队长带了备用「护腿板」，给忘带自己护腿板的球员。

words.enDefinition: A film much shorter than a typical feature film.

examples.en: We watched a short film before the director came out to answer our questions.
examples.zh: 导演出来回答问题前，我们看了一部「电影短片」。

examples.en: My roommate made a short film about the people who work in our library.
examples.zh: 室友拍了一部关于图书馆工作人员的「电影短片」。

words.enDefinition: improvised performance made up of short separate scenes or games

examples.en: The group began with short-form improv before trying a longer story together.
examples.zh: 这组人先做了「短形式即兴表演」，再合演一个更长的故事。

examples.en: We tried short-form improv at a workshop run by two older students.
examples.zh: 两位高年级同学办的工作坊上，我们尝试了「短形式即兴表演」。

words.enDefinition: a book containing a number of short fictional works

examples.en: I packed a short story collection for a quiet afternoon outside.
examples.zh: 我带了本「短篇小说集」，准备在户外安静地看一下午。

examples.en: The book club chose one piece from the short story collection for discussion.
examples.zh: 读书会从这本「短篇小说集」里选了一篇来讨论。

collocations: a piece from a short story collection

words.enDefinition: a timer showing the time a basketball team has left to attempt a legal shot

examples.en: The shot clock showed just two seconds when the pass reached the corner.
examples.zh: 传球到角落时，「进攻计时器」只剩两秒。

examples.en: We could see the shot clock clearly from the seats above the far basket.
examples.zh: 从另一端篮筐上方的座位，可以清楚看到「进攻计时器」。

words.enDefinition: a shot going toward the goal that would score if it were not stopped

examples.en: The goalkeeper saved our first shot on target just before the break.
examples.zh: 中场休息前，守门员扑出了我们第一脚「射正」的球。

examples.en: Our only shot on target came in the opening minutes of the second half.
examples.zh: 我们唯一一次「射正」发生在下半场开始后的几分钟。

words.enDefinition: a control button along the upper edge of a game controller

examples.en: The tutorial showed a shoulder button for switching between the two toolbars.
examples.zh: 教程显示可以用一个「手柄肩键」在两个工具栏间切换。

examples.en: I pressed the shoulder button while trying out the new controller layout.
examples.zh: 试用新的手柄布局时，我按了一下「手柄肩键」。

collocations: the shoulder button on a gamepad

words.enDefinition: a song originally written for a stage musical

examples.en: My classmate sang a show tune at the end of our workshop.
examples.zh: 工作坊最后，同学唱了一首「音乐剧歌曲」。

examples.en: I recognised the show tune from a recording of last year's musical.
examples.zh: 我听过去年的音乐剧录音，认出了这首「音乐剧歌曲」。

words.enDefinition: The advertised time at which a particular movie showing is due to start.

examples.en: I checked the showtime because my class was due to finish at half past six.
examples.zh: 我那节课要到六点半才下课，所以查了「电影开场时间」。

examples.en: The latest showtime was too late for anyone who needed the last bus back.
examples.zh: 要赶末班公交回去的人觉得，最后一场的「电影开场时间」太晚了。

words.enDefinition: a playback mode that plays tracks in a different order from the displayed list

examples.en: I switched to shuffle play after hearing the first few tracks in order.
examples.zh: 按顺序听过开头几首后，我切到了「随机顺序播放」。

examples.en: The app returned to shuffle play when I reopened it on the bus.
examples.zh: 我在公交上重新打开音乐应用时，应用回到了「随机顺序播放」。

words.enDefinition: to mix the order of the cards before playing

examples.en: We needed to shuffle the deck again before the next round began.
examples.zh: 下一轮开始前，我们得再「洗牌」。

examples.en: My classmate offered to shuffle the deck while everyone chose a seat.
examples.zh: 大家找座位时，同学主动说来「洗牌」。

collocations: ask someone to shuffle the deck

words.enDefinition: the control pressed to take a photograph

examples.en: I found the shutter button after borrowing my friend's old camera.
examples.zh: 借到朋友的旧相机后，我找到了「快门按钮」。

examples.en: The shutter button felt different from the one on my phone.
examples.zh: 「快门按钮」按起来和我手机上的不太一样。

words.enDefinition: the duration for which a camera exposes the film or sensor

examples.en: I compared how shutter speed changed the look of water in my photos.
examples.zh: 我对比了「快门速度」如何改变照片里水的效果。

examples.en: My friend explained shutter speed while we sorted the pictures we had taken.
examples.zh: 我们整理拍好的照片时，朋友给我讲了「快门速度」。

words.enDefinition: the light object with a skirt of feathers or plastic hit in badminton

examples.en: We found a shuttlecock under the bench after our first badminton game that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午羽毛球第一场结束后，我们在长凳下找到一个「羽毛球」。

examples.en: My classmate picked up the shuttlecock and handed it back to the server.
examples.zh: 同学捡起「羽毛球」，交还给发球人。

words.enDefinition: to read and perform a piece from its score without preparing it in advance

examples.en: We had to sight-read music for a short exercise in the campus choir rehearsal.
examples.zh: 校园合唱团排练时有项简短练习，需要我们「视谱演唱」。

examples.en: My classmate can sight-read music on piano much faster than I can these days.
examples.zh: 最近我同学用钢琴「视谱演奏」比我快得多。

words.enDefinition: a show where an interpreter renders the dialogue in sign language

examples.en: The interpreter stood beside the stage throughout the sign-interpreted performance that evening.
examples.zh: 当晚「有手语传译的演出」期间，译员全程站在舞台旁。

examples.en: We checked which evening shows had a sign-interpreted performance listed online.
examples.zh: 我们在网上查找晚间场次中哪些是「有手语传译的演出」。

words.enDefinition: A film made without recorded dialogue synchronized to what happens on screen.

examples.en: The campus cinema showed a silent film with live piano music on Friday evening.
examples.zh: 星期五晚上，校园影院放了一部「无声电影」，有钢琴现场配乐。

examples.en: We studied a silent film that conveyed an awkward reunion entirely through expressions and gestures.
examples.zh: 我们分析了一部「无声电影」，片中一次尴尬的重逢全靠表情和动作来表现。

collocations: live music for a silent film

words.enDefinition: an occasion when people are invited to sing together, often to familiar music

examples.en: The music society hosted a sing-along in the courtyard after the performance had ended.
examples.zh: 演出结束后，音乐社在庭院里办了场「集体跟唱活动」。

examples.en: The chorus became a sing-along as most people in the room knew the words.
examples.zh: 屋里大多数人都会唱，副歌时就出现了「集体跟唱」。

words.enDefinition: to sing at the correct pitches for the music

examples.en: It was easier to sing in tune once I could hear the piano clearly.
examples.zh: 能听清伴奏钢琴后，我更容易「唱得不跑调」。

examples.en: Our friend helped us sing in tune by playing the first notes before rehearsal.
examples.zh: 排练前，朋友弹了开头几个音，帮我们「唱得不跑调」。

collocations: be able to sing in tune

words.enDefinition: a ticket valid on one day of a multi-day event

examples.en: I bought a single-day ticket because I was only free on Sunday.
examples.zh: 我只有周日有空，所以买了张「单日门票」。

examples.en: The single-day ticket covered every race on the selected day of competition.
examples.zh: 「单日门票」涵盖所选比赛日的每场赛跑。

words.enDefinition: a ticket for one game rather than multiple games

examples.en: I wanted a single-game ticket because my sister was visiting for one weekend.
examples.zh: 我想买张「单场比赛门票」，因为妹妹只来一个周末。

examples.en: The single-game ticket for Sunday's game was still available after class.
examples.zh: 下课后，周日比赛的「单场比赛门票」仍可购买。

words.enDefinition: an option designed for one person to play alone

examples.en: I tried single-player mode while everyone else was still on the way.
examples.zh: 其他人还在路上，我先试了「单人模式」。

examples.en: The game opens in single-player mode unless you select a group option.
examples.zh: 这个游戏默认打开「单人模式」，也可以选多人选项。

words.enDefinition: to spend part or all of a game waiting without taking part

examples.en: I expected to sit on the bench until the start of the second half.
examples.zh: 我以为要一直「坐在替补席上」等到下半场开始。

examples.en: She preferred to play briefly rather than sit on the bench for the entire match.
examples.zh: 她宁可短暂上场，也不想整场都「坐在替补席上」。

collocations: have to sit on the bench
sit on the bench for a game
wait to play while you sit on the bench

words.enDefinition: A comedy series built around recurring characters and the situations they regularly get into.

examples.en: My flatmate put on a sitcom set in a small radio station downtown.
examples.zh: 室友放了一部「情景喜剧」，故事发生在市中心一家小电台。

examples.en: The situation comedy used the same handful of characters even when the location changed.
examples.zh: 这部「情景喜剧」切换场景时，出场的还是同样那几个人。

words.enDefinition: Comedy presented as a series of separate short comic scenes.

examples.en: The streaming service listed the show under sketch comedy because each scene had different characters.
examples.zh: 每场戏角色各不相同，所以流媒体平台把这档节目列在「短剧喜剧」下面。

examples.en: A friend likes sketch comedy because one funny scene is easy to watch between classes.
examples.zh: 有位朋友喜欢「短剧喜剧」，因为课间看一个搞笑场景很方便。

words.enDefinition: a notebook of paper used for sketches or drawings

examples.en: I brought a sketchbook to the café so I could draw between classes.
examples.zh: 我带了本「速写本」去咖啡馆，好在课间画几笔。

examples.en: My sketchbook filled up during the weeks we spent drawing outdoors.
examples.zh: 我们外出写生的那几周，我把「速写本」画满了。

words.enDefinition: A player control for moving past a show's opening title or theme sequence.

examples.en: We used “Skip intro” after watching the opening credits in the first episode that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚看过第一集的片头后，我们用了「跳过片头」。

examples.en: The skip intro button appeared as soon as the familiar theme music started playing.
examples.zh: 熟悉的主题音乐一响起，「跳过片头」按钮就出现了。

words.enDefinition: A story that builds interest or tension gradually over a relatively long time.

examples.en: My roommate called the series a slow burn because the big questions came much later.
examples.zh: 室友说这部剧是「慢热型作品」，因为几个大疑问到后面才抛出来。

examples.en: The film was a slow burn, but by the end I cared about every character.
examples.zh: 这部电影是「慢热型作品」，看到最后我已经很在意每个角色。

collocations: a slow burn with a strong ending
a film that is a slow burn
describe a show as a slow burn

words.enDefinition: a musician who releases or performs music under their own name

examples.en: She returned as a solo artist after spending two years in a band.
examples.zh: 她在乐队演出了两年，之后以「个人名义表演的艺人」身份重返舞台。

examples.en: The solo artist played several songs on guitar before inviting her friends up.
examples.zh: 那位「个人名义表演的艺人」边弹吉他边唱了几首歌，才请朋友们上台。

collocations: launch a career as a solo artist

words.enDefinition: a request from a listener asking for a particular song to be performed

examples.en: The singer took a song request from someone sitting beside us that night.
examples.zh: 那晚，歌手接受了坐在我们旁边的一位观众的「点歌请求」。

examples.en: I wrote a song request on a card and left it near the stage.
examples.zh: 我把「点歌请求」写在卡片上，留在了舞台旁。

words.enDefinition: a book containing the words, musical notation, or both for a set of songs

examples.en: The library's songbook included a shorter version of the piece we were learning.
examples.zh: 图书馆那本「歌曲集」里有我们在学的曲子的简短版。

examples.en: I borrowed a songbook from my roommate before going to the student choir rehearsal.
examples.zh: 去学生合唱团排练之前，我向室友借了一本「歌曲集」。

words.enDefinition: a person who writes music or words for songs

examples.en: A songwriter from the university performed several of his own pieces at the café.
examples.zh: 一位校内「歌曲创作者」在咖啡馆演唱了几首自己的作品。

examples.en: The songwriter told us that the melody came first and the words much later.
examples.zh: 「歌曲创作者」告诉我们，先有旋律，很久之后才写歌词。

words.enDefinition: a signal for music or an effect to begin or change

examples.en: The stage manager called the sound cue for the doorbell during rehearsal.
examples.zh: 排练时，舞台监督发出「音效提示」，让门铃声响起。

examples.en: We repeated the sound cue because the rain effect started too early.
examples.zh: 模拟下雨的声音放早了，我们又过了一遍「音效提示」。

words.enDefinition: a person who sets up, controls, or records sound for performances

examples.en: The sound engineer asked the band to play the loudest part before the doors opened.
examples.zh: 开门前，「音响工程师」请乐队演奏声音最大的那一段。

examples.en: I sat near the sound engineer during our society's outdoor concert that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚我们社团办户外音乐会时，我坐在「音响工程师」附近。

words.enDefinition: a test of sound equipment and performance levels before a show

examples.en: The guitarist played two chords during soundcheck before the venue opened to the public that evening.
examples.zh: 当晚场馆开放前，吉他手在「演出前试音」时弹了两个和弦。

examples.en: I heard part of the soundcheck while waiting outside with the other students.
examples.zh: 我和其他学生在外面等时，听见了一部分「演出前试音」。

words.enDefinition: The recorded sound or music associated with a film, show, or other production.

examples.en: I looked up the soundtrack because I wanted to hear the opening song again.
examples.zh: 我查了这部片的「影视原声」，因为想再听一遍片头曲。

examples.en: The soundtrack got quieter just before the character opened the door to the old workshop.
examples.zh: 角色快要打开旧工作室门的时候，「影视原声」变小了。

words.enDefinition: an album of music associated with a film, show, or similar production

examples.en: I saved the soundtrack album after watching the film at the campus cinema.
examples.zh: 在校园电影院看完电影后，我收藏了「原声音乐专辑」。

examples.en: The soundtrack album had several pieces that only appeared briefly in the film.
examples.zh: 「原声音乐专辑」里有几首曲子在电影中只短暂出现过。

words.enDefinition: an option to watch a game without controlling a player

examples.en: I switched to spectator mode when all the places were already taken.
examples.zh: 玩家名额都满了，我就切换到「观战模式」。

examples.en: My roommate used spectator mode to watch how we solved the final puzzle.
examples.zh: 室友用「观战模式」看我们是怎么解开最后一道谜题的。

words.enDefinition: using separate areas of one display for different players' views

examples.en: The split-screen view gave each of us room to see our own path.
examples.zh: 「分屏」画面让我们各自有空间看自己的路线。

examples.en: We tried a split-screen session after connecting the second controller to the console.
examples.zh: 给主机接上第二个手柄后，我们试着用「分屏」玩了一局。

words.enDefinition: A warning that the next part of a discussion reveals an important story detail.

examples.en: The reviewer gave a spoiler alert before talking about the last scene in detail.
examples.zh: 影评人在细讲最后一场戏之前先发了个「剧透提醒」。

examples.en: My classmate put a spoiler alert above her message about what happened in the episode.
examples.zh: 同学发消息聊这一集演了什么前，先在上面写了「剧透提醒」。

collocations: a spoiler alert before the review

words.enDefinition: Information that reveals an important event that a viewer might want to discover for themselves.

examples.en: I saw a spoiler while looking up the name of one of the actors.
examples.zh: 我查其中一位演员的名字时看到了一条「剧透」。

examples.en: The first paragraph of the review had a spoiler for anyone who missed the finale.
examples.zh: 对还没看终集的人来说，影评第一段里就有「剧透」。

words.enDefinition: a live performance of poetry or expressive writing spoken aloud

examples.en: I attended a spoken-word performance where students shared poetry about their hometowns.
examples.zh: 我参加了一场「口语诗表演」，同学们朗诵了写家乡的诗。

examples.en: Her spoken-word performance used pauses to make the words stand out.
examples.zh: 她在「口语诗表演」中用停顿来突出一些词。

words.enDefinition: fair and respectful conduct toward other players and officials in sport

examples.en: The referee praised the sportsmanship both teams showed at the end of the match.
examples.zh: 裁判表扬了两队赛后都体现出的「体育精神」。

examples.en: Our club gives a prize for sportsmanship at the end of each campus tournament.
examples.zh: 我们社团每次校园锦标赛结束时都会颁发「体育精神」奖。

words.enDefinition: someone who controls a spotlight that follows performers onstage

examples.en: The spotlight operator met with us before we went through the ending.
examples.zh: 我们走排结尾段之前，「追光灯操作员」先和我们碰了个面。

examples.en: My roommate volunteered as a spotlight operator for the drama club this term.
examples.zh: 室友这学期自愿担任戏剧社的「追光灯操作员」。

words.enDefinition: A gym frame with supports intended to hold a barbell at different heights.

examples.en: The new squat rack was marked on the plan beside the entrance to the weight room.
examples.zh: 「深蹲架」是新的，标在力量训练室入口旁的平面图上。

examples.en: I asked the instructor which part of the diagram showed the squat rack near the window.
examples.zh: 我问教练，图里哪一部分画的是窗边的「深蹲架」。

collocations: a squat rack in the weight room

words.enDefinition: A large inflatable exercise ball used in some balance and fitness activities.

examples.en: The studio kept a stability ball in a high rack beside the storage cupboard.
examples.zh: 团课教室把一个「健身平衡球」放在储物柜旁的高架上。

examples.en: I noticed the stability ball in the diagram of equipment available for group fitness.
examples.zh: 我在团课可用器材的示意图中留意到了「健身平衡球」。

collocations: a stability ball in the studio

words.enDefinition: a diagram showing the numbered areas within a sports stadium

examples.en: I used the stadium section map to find the entrance closest to my seats.
examples.zh: 我用「体育场分区图」找离座位最近的入口。

examples.en: The stadium section map showed the student area on the side nearest campus.
examples.zh: 「体育场分区图」显示学生区在靠近校园的那一侧。

collocations: look at a stadium section map

words.enDefinition: a version of an existing story created to be performed onstage

examples.en: Our class watched a stage adaptation of a novel we had just finished.
examples.zh: 我们班看了一部「舞台改编作品」，原著是刚读完的一本小说。

examples.en: The stage adaptation used just two actors to tell the entire story.
examples.zh: 这部「舞台改编作品」只用两位演员就讲完了整个故事。

words.enDefinition: a planned instant or brief period of darkness during a production

examples.en: The stage blackout separated the scene in the flat from the street scene.
examples.zh: 「舞台灯光全熄」把公寓里的戏和街头那场戏隔开了。

examples.en: The audience fell quiet as soon as the stage blackout began.
examples.zh: 「舞台灯光全熄」一开始，观众就安静了下来。

words.enDefinition: an instruction in a script about action, movement, or staging

examples.en: The stage direction said to pause before the next actor entered the room.
examples.zh: 「舞台指示」要求在下一位演员进屋前停顿一下。

examples.en: I marked a stage direction in my script so I wouldn't miss it.
examples.zh: 我在剧本上标出一处「舞台指示」，免得漏掉。

words.enDefinition: the act of coming onto the stage during a performance

examples.en: The actor's stage entrance was meant to happen while the lights were still low.
examples.zh: 原定这位演员要在灯光还很暗时「登场」。

examples.en: I marked my stage entrance in the margin next to my first line.
examples.zh: 我在第一句台词旁边的空白处标出了自己的「登场」时机。

words.enDefinition: the act of leaving the stage during a performance

examples.en: The performer timed her stage exit with the last beat of the music.
examples.zh: 那位表演者掐准音乐最后一拍「退场」。

examples.en: Our director moved one chair so the stage exit looked more natural.
examples.zh: 导演挪了一把椅子，让「退场」看起来更自然。

words.enDefinition: the left side of the stage from the position of a performer facing the audience

examples.en: The singer entered from stage left as the lights came up after the break.
examples.zh: 休息过后舞台灯亮了，歌手从「演员视角的舞台左侧」上场。

examples.en: The guitarist waited at stage left until the rest of the band was ready.
examples.zh: 吉他手在「演员视角的舞台左侧」等乐队其他成员准备好。

words.enDefinition: makeup used to shape a performer's appearance for an audience

examples.en: The actors could see their stage makeup clearly under the rehearsal lights.
examples.zh: 演员在排练灯光下能清楚看见自己的「舞台妆」。

examples.en: I removed my stage makeup before getting the bus back to campus.
examples.zh: 我先卸掉「舞台妆」，然后坐公交回学校。

words.enDefinition: the person who coordinates rehearsals and keeps a live performance running

examples.en: The stage manager reminded us when we needed to be ready to enter.
examples.zh: 「舞台监督」提醒我们什么时候该为上场做好准备。

examples.en: I watched the stage manager make notes during our first full run.
examples.zh: 第一次完整走排时，我看着「舞台监督」记下了要点。

words.enDefinition: a speaker that lets performers hear themselves or other players onstage

examples.en: The singer asked for a little more piano in her stage monitor before starting.
examples.zh: 唱之前，歌手请把她的「舞台返听音箱」里的钢琴声调大一些。

examples.en: The technician moved the stage monitor away from the edge of the platform.
examples.zh: 音响技术人员把「舞台返听音箱」从台子边挪开了。

words.enDefinition: a piece of drama written to be performed by actors onstage

examples.en: The students wrote a stage play about strangers waiting for the same bus.
examples.zh: 同学们写了一部「舞台剧」，讲几个陌生人等同一班公交的故事。

examples.en: I had only seen the film before watching the stage play on campus.
examples.zh: 我以前只看过电影，后来才在学校看到这部「舞台剧」。

words.enDefinition: a performer's ability to hold an audience's attention on stage

examples.en: Our friend had great stage presence even though it was her first solo show.
examples.zh: 虽然是第一次独唱演出，朋友的「舞台表现力」已经很强。

examples.en: The tutor asked what gave the singer such strong stage presence during the final song.
examples.zh: 导师问，这位歌手在最后一首歌里为什么会有那么强的「舞台表现力」。

words.enDefinition: an object used by a performer during a stage production

examples.en: The umbrella was a stage prop from an earlier student production.
examples.zh: 那把伞是之前一部学生剧用过的「舞台道具」。

examples.en: I borrowed a stage prop that looked exactly like my old suitcase.
examples.zh: 我借了一件和我的旧行李箱一模一样的「舞台道具」。

words.enDefinition: the right side of the stage from the position of a performer facing the audience

examples.en: The keyboard stayed at stage right while the first performer sang by herself.
examples.zh: 第一位表演者独唱时，键盘放在「演员视角的舞台右侧」。

examples.en: The host pointed to stage right and introduced the student players from the jazz society.
examples.zh: 主持人指向「演员视角的舞台右侧」，介绍了爵士社的学生乐手。

words.zhGloss: 故意让观众听见的耳语
words.enDefinition: a loud whisper intended to be heard by the audience
acceptedZhAnswers: 故意让观众听见的耳语

examples.en: The actor used a stage whisper so we could hear the secret.
examples.zh: 演员用「故意让观众听见的耳语」把秘密说了出来。

examples.en: Her stage whisper was the only sound in the theatre for a moment.
examples.zh: 一时间，剧场里唯一的声音就是她「故意让观众听见的耳语」。

words.enDefinition: a public presentation of a script with limited staging and movement

examples.en: The club held a staged reading before deciding whether to produce the play.
examples.zh: 社团先办了一场「剧本朗读演出」，再决定要不要正式演出。

examples.en: At the staged reading, the performers used chairs and did not wear costumes.
examples.zh: 「剧本朗读演出」时，表演者用了椅子，没有穿戏服。

collocations: staged reading of a new play

words.enDefinition: A machine that provides exercise using moving steps or pedals that imitate climbing stairs.

examples.en: The stair climber was easy to recognize because it looked like a short moving staircase.
examples.zh: 「登阶机」很容易认，因为看起来像一小段会动的楼梯。

examples.en: We saw a notice about the stair climber while waiting for the tour to start.
examples.zh: 我们在等参观开始时，看到了一则关于「登阶机」的告示。

words.enDefinition: An episode with a self-contained story that viewers can follow without seeing the others.

examples.en: My roommate recommended a stand-alone episode because I had missed the rest of the season.
examples.zh: 室友推荐了「剧情独立的一集」，因为我没看这一季的其他集。

examples.en: We finished a stand-alone episode while waiting for another friend to get back from class.
examples.zh: 我们等另一位朋友下课回来时，看完了「剧情独立的一集」。

words.enDefinition: a form of live comedy usually performed by one person speaking

examples.en: The college hosted a night of stand-up comedy by students and local performers.
examples.zh: 学院办了一场「单口喜剧」之夜，由学生和本地表演者上台。

examples.en: I tried stand-up comedy because I wanted to make my classmates laugh.
examples.zh: 我尝试表演「单口喜剧」，因为想逗同学笑。

words.enDefinition: a line of people waiting for space to become available

examples.en: My friends waited in the standby line outside the lecture hall for tickets.
examples.zh: 朋友们在讲堂外的「现场候补队伍」里等着有没有票。

examples.en: They moved the standby line indoors when the rain started that evening.
examples.zh: 那天晚上开始下雨，工作人员让「现场候补队伍」移到屋里。

words.enDefinition: a performer kept available to replace a principal actor when needed

examples.en: The standby performer waited backstage in case the lead singer could not continue.
examples.zh: 「随时待命的替补演员」在后台等着，以防主唱不能继续演出。

examples.en: One standby performer learned the lead role without taking a regular ensemble part.
examples.zh: 有一位「随时待命的替补演员」排练了主角的戏份，平时在这出戏里没有固定角色。

words.enDefinition: enthusiastic applause from audience members standing rather than sitting

examples.en: The student cast received a standing ovation after the closing performance.
examples.zh: 收官演出结束后，观众向学生演员们「起立鼓掌致敬」。

examples.en: I joined the standing ovation because my roommate had danced so well.
examples.zh: 室友跳得太好了，我也跟着大家一起「起立鼓掌致敬」。

words.enDefinition: a tiered spectator area with space to stand instead of seats

examples.en: We watched the match from a standing terrace near one corner.
examples.zh: 我们站在靠近一个角落的「阶梯式站席看台」上看比赛。

examples.en: The standing terrace was clearly marked on the stadium seating plan.
examples.zh: 体育场座位图上清楚标出了「阶梯式站席看台」。

words.enDefinition: a ticket that lets its holder watch from a standing area

examples.en: We chose a standing ticket because we wanted to stay near the stage.
examples.zh: 我们想离舞台近一点，就选了「站席票」。

examples.en: The standing ticket cost less than a seat on the upper level.
examples.zh: 「站席票」比上层看台的座票便宜。

words.enDefinition: watching the night sky as a leisure activity

examples.en: We tried stargazing after the clouds moved away from the park.
examples.zh: 公园上空的云散开后，我们试着「观星」。

examples.en: My roommate enjoys stargazing when the sky is clear after dinner.
examples.zh: 晚饭后天空晴朗时，室友喜欢「观星」。

words.enDefinition: the five basketball players selected to begin a game for one team

examples.en: Our starting five stood near the centre circle while waiting for the game to begin.
examples.zh: 我们的「篮球首发五人」在中圈附近等比赛开始。

examples.en: The coach changed the starting five after our usual point guard missed the bus.
examples.zh: 平时打控卫的队员没赶上公交，教练调整了「篮球首发五人」。

words.enDefinition: the cards a player receives at the beginning

examples.en: I looked at my starting hand before deciding how to begin.
examples.zh: 我先看了自己的「起手牌」，才决定怎么开局。

examples.en: The guide showed how many cards belonged in the starting hand.
examples.zh: 指南写着「起手牌」有几张。

words.enDefinition: the players selected to begin a match

examples.en: The coach announced the starting lineup before our classmates arrived to watch the match.
examples.zh: 同学来观赛前，教练宣布了「首发阵容」。

examples.en: I was surprised to see our newest player in the starting lineup that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，我没想到在「首发阵容」里看到了新队员。

words.enDefinition: the player who acts first in a game or round

examples.en: We picked a starting player before looking at any of the cards.
examples.zh: 我们在看牌之前先选了个「先手玩家」。

examples.en: The starting player read out the first clue for the whole group.
examples.zh: 「先手玩家」把第一条线索念给了大家。

collocations: a marker for the starting player
the starting player for this round

words.enDefinition: A bicycle-like exercise machine designed to stay in one place while a person pedals.

examples.en: The stationary bike nearest the door had a display with several different language options.
examples.zh: 离门最近的那台「固定式健身车」屏幕上有几种语言选项。

examples.en: My classmate recognized a stationary bike like the one in her old residence hall.
examples.zh: 同学认出了一台「固定式健身车」，跟她以前宿舍楼里的很像。

collocations: a stationary bike in the studio

words.enDefinition: to keep behaving like the character you are portraying

examples.en: It was hard to stay in character when someone dropped the prop phone.
examples.zh: 有人把道具电话掉在地上时，很难「保持角色状态」。

examples.en: My partner managed to stay in character even though half the cast laughed.
examples.zh: 虽然半数演员都笑了，搭档还是「保持了角色状态」。

collocations: stay in character throughout a scene

words.enDefinition: to remain at a game until the referee ends it

examples.en: We chose to stay until the final whistle because the score was still close.
examples.zh: 因为比分咬得很紧，我们决定「待到终场哨响」。

examples.en: My roommate wanted to stay until the final whistle even though it was cold.
examples.zh: 虽然天冷，室友还是想「待到终场哨响」。

collocations: want to stay until the final whistle
decide to stay until the final whistle
plan to stay until the final whistle

words.enDefinition: A level of physical effort that stays fairly even as an activity continues.

examples.en: I recorded a steady effort in my log because the whole walk felt evenly paced.
examples.zh: 因为整段路都走得很均匀，我在日志里记下了「持续均匀的用力」。

examples.en: My roommate described the second half of the session as a steady effort in her notes.
examples.zh: 室友在笔记里把课程后半段记为「持续均匀的用力」。

collocations: record steady effort in a log

words.enDefinition: A form of group aerobic exercise using a low platform, often with music.

examples.en: The student newsletter listed step aerobics among the lunchtime classes in the main building.
examples.zh: 学生简报把「有氧踏板操」列为主楼的午间课程之一。

examples.en: The room used for step aerobics was just past the large studio with mirrors.
examples.zh: 上「有氧踏板操」的房间就在有镜子的大教室过去一点。

words.enDefinition: The total number of steps recorded during a period or an activity.

examples.en: I checked my step count after walking around the campus track with my roommate.
examples.zh: 我跟室友绕校园跑道走完后，查了自己的「步数」。

examples.en: The app showed my step count beside the time I had spent walking indoors.
examples.zh: 应用在我室内步行时间的旁边显示了「步数」。

words.enDefinition: A raised, flat exercise platform used in some group fitness classes.

examples.en: The instructor marked a place on the floor for each step platform before class.
examples.zh: 上课前，教练在地板上标出了每块「健身踏板」的位置。

examples.en: The step platform was stored next to the mats in our campus recreation studio.
examples.zh: 我们校园文体教室的「健身踏板」放在垫子旁边。

words.enDefinition: art depicting arranged objects that do not move on their own

examples.en: We painted a still life with mugs from the student kitchen.
examples.zh: 我们用学生厨房里的马克杯布置场景，画了幅「静物画」。

examples.en: I moved the apple closer to the lamp for my still life.
examples.zh: 我画「静物画」时，把苹果往台灯旁挪了挪。

words.enDefinition: a small marker used to identify a position in knitting or crochet

examples.en: I placed a stitch marker where the repeated section was supposed to begin.
examples.zh: 我在重复段落开始的位置放了个「针目记号扣」。

examples.en: The red stitch marker made the start of the row easy to find.
examples.zh: 红色「针目记号扣」让我很容易找到一行的开头。

words.enDefinition: Animation made by photographing objects in slightly different positions frame by frame.

examples.en: The short used stop-motion animation to make a desk lamp look like it could walk.
examples.zh: 这部短片用「定格动画」让台灯看起来像会走路。

examples.en: We saw a display about stop-motion animation beside the costumes at the campus film exhibition.
examples.zh: 在校园电影展上，我们在戏服旁边看到了介绍「定格动画」的展品。

words.enDefinition: time added at the end of a half to allow for time lost during play

examples.en: The referee indicated stoppage time just as many of the students began to leave.
examples.zh: 不少学生刚开始离开，裁判就示意进入「伤停补时」。

examples.en: The winning goal came during stoppage time after neither team had scored for an hour.
examples.zh: 两队有一小时没进球，「伤停补时」阶段才出现制胜进球。

words.enDefinition: a way of playing organised around a game narrative

examples.en: I saved story mode for the weekend when I had more time.
examples.zh: 我把「剧情模式」留到周末时间多一点的时候再玩。

examples.en: The next chapter in story mode opened after we solved the puzzle.
examples.zh: 我们解开谜题后，「剧情模式」的下一章就开放了。

words.enDefinition: The central situation or idea on which a story is built.

examples.en: The story premise sounded ordinary until I learned that the whole plot happened in one day.
examples.zh: 后来我才知道整个情节都发生在一天内，先前还觉得这个「故事基本设定」很普通。

examples.en: My roommate liked the story premise but thought the opening could have been shorter.
examples.zh: 室友喜欢这个「故事基本设定」，不过觉得开头可以更短一些。

collocations: a story premise for a film

words.enDefinition: The sequence of events forming a story or a thread within it.

examples.en: I could follow the storyline even though I had missed the first few minutes.
examples.zh: 虽然错过了开头几分钟，我还是能跟上「故事线」。

examples.en: The storyline about the sisters kept me watching after the campus scenes began to repeat.
examples.zh: 后来校园里一些场景开始重复，但姐妹俩的「故事线」让我继续看了下去。

collocations: bring a storyline to an end

words.enDefinition: a way of winning a tennis match without losing a set

examples.en: My classmate won in straight sets even though the second set was very close.
examples.zh: 虽然第二盘打得很接近，同学还是「未失一盘」赢得比赛。

examples.en: The college pair lost in straight sets but saved several set points along the way.
examples.zh: 学院这对组合「一盘没赢」就输了，不过过程中挽救了几个盘点。

words.enDefinition: To watch or deliver a video stream at high-definition picture quality.

examples.en: We chose to stream in HD when the details in the landscape mattered to us.
examples.zh: 风景细节对我们很重要，所以我们选了「以高清画质在线播放」。

examples.en: I checked whether we could stream in HD on the screen in our common room.
examples.zh: 我查了公共休息室的屏幕能不能「以高清画质在线播放」。

collocations: an option to stream in HD

words.enDefinition: The collection of films and shows offered by an online viewing service.

examples.en: I browsed the streaming catalog looking for a comedy short enough to watch before class.
examples.zh: 我翻了翻「流媒体片库」，想找部能在上课前看完的短喜剧。

examples.en: The streaming catalog had several documentaries from the same director under different category labels.
examples.zh: 「流媒体片库」有同一位导演的几部纪录片，放在不同的分类下面。

collocations: add a film to the streaming catalog

words.enDefinition: A film or show produced or commissioned specifically for a streaming service.

examples.en: The film club chose a streaming original for its discussion about how series are made.
examples.zh: 电影社选了一部「流媒体原创作品」，用来讨论剧集是怎么制作的。

examples.en: My classmate recommended a streaming original that had been filmed in her hometown that summer.
examples.zh: 同学推荐了一部「流媒体原创作品」，是那个夏天在她家乡拍的。

words.enDefinition: An online service that delivers media for playback over an internet connection.

examples.en: We checked which streaming service carried the documentary our tutor had mentioned in class.
examples.zh: 我们查了哪家「流媒体服务」可以看导师上课提过的那部纪录片。

examples.en: The streaming service offered two different versions of the film we wanted to watch.
examples.zh: 这家「流媒体服务」提供了我们想看的电影的两个不同版本。

collocations: a show on a streaming service

words.enDefinition: making photographs of ordinary scenes in public streets or spaces

examples.en: I tried street photography during a quiet morning near campus.
examples.zh: 我选了个安静的早晨，在学校附近试了试「街头摄影」。

examples.en: Our workshop on street photography focused on signs, reflections and shopfronts.
examples.zh: 我们的「街头摄影」工作坊主要拍招牌、倒影和店面。

words.enDefinition: A class focused on activities that train the muscles to produce force.

examples.en: The timetable described the strength class as a group session with several kinds of equipment.
examples.zh: 时间表把「力量训练课」介绍为使用多种器材的团课。

examples.en: My roommate asked how to find the strength class on the recreation center's website.
examples.zh: 室友问，怎么在校园文体中心的网站上找到「力量训练课」。

collocations: a strength class in the fitness studio

words.enDefinition: Exercise intended to develop the ability of muscles to produce force.

examples.en: My classmate asked where strength training appeared on the new group fitness schedule this term.
examples.zh: 同学问，这学期新的团课时间表上「力量训练」列在哪儿。

examples.en: The studio listed strength training separately from the classes held in the pool downstairs.
examples.zh: 团课教室把「力量训练」和楼下泳池里上的课分开列出。

collocations: a class focused on strength training

words.enDefinition: canvas pulled tight over a frame for painting

examples.en: My roommate propped a stretched canvas on the easel by the window.
examples.zh: 室友把一块「绷好的画布」架在窗边的画架上。

examples.en: The studio gave each beginner a small stretched canvas for the afternoon session.
examples.zh: 画室给每位新手发了一块小「绷好的画布」，供下午活动用。

words.enDefinition: A space set aside for people to stretch in a gym or studio.

examples.en: The stretching area had floor mats lined up on a shelf beside the mirror.
examples.zh: 「拉伸区」的镜子旁有个架子，上面整齐摆着垫子。

examples.en: Our guide pointed out the stretching area after we walked past the row of bikes.
examples.zh: 经过那一排健身车后，向导指给我们看「拉伸区」。

words.enDefinition: A class focused on exercises that stretch different parts of the body.

examples.en: Our instructor moved the stretching class downstairs when the main studio was being cleaned.
examples.zh: 主教室在打扫时，教练把「拉伸课」移到了楼下。

examples.en: The campus notice said the stretching class would take place after the break for lunch.
examples.zh: 校园告示写着，「拉伸课」会在午休后上。

words.enDefinition: to take down and remove scenery after a production

examples.en: We stayed to strike the set after the last performance on Saturday night.
examples.zh: 周六晚最后一场演出结束后，我们留下来「拆除舞台布景」。

examples.en: The company planned to strike the set before the next group moved in.
examples.zh: 剧团计划在下一组人进来之前「拆除舞台布景」。

words.enDefinition: a baseball outcome when the batter receives a third strike

examples.en: The crowd applauded the pitcher after the strikeout on the last pitch of the inning.
examples.zh: 这一局最后一球造成「三振」后，观众为投手鼓掌。

examples.en: The score sheet recorded a strikeout beside the first batter's name that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，计分表在第一位击球手的名字旁记了一次「三振」。

words.enDefinition: to put a thread or cord through beads to join them

examples.en: We sat by the window to string beads in the afternoon light.
examples.zh: 我们坐在窗边，借午后的光「把珠子串起来」。

examples.en: My roommate likes to string beads while listening to an old playlist.
examples.zh: 室友喜欢听旧歌单时「把珠子串起来」。

words.enDefinition: a phrase used when a tune or thought keeps repeating in your mind

examples.en: That chorus was stuck in my head all afternoon while I worked in the library.
examples.zh: 我下午在图书馆干活时，那段副歌一直「在我脑海里挥之不去」。

examples.en: The song from our performance is still stuck in my head from last night.
examples.zh: 我们昨晚演的那首歌现在还「在我脑海里挥之不去」。

words.enDefinition: an entry point specifically designated for students attending an event

examples.en: We followed the signs to the student entrance behind the gym.
examples.zh: 我们跟着标牌走到体育馆后面的「学生专用入口」。

examples.en: My friend waited near the student entrance while I found our tickets.
examples.zh: 我找票时，朋友在「学生专用入口」附近等着。

words.enDefinition: a pass allowing a student to bring a guest to an event

examples.en: I asked if a student guest pass was available for my flatmate.
examples.zh: 我问能不能给室友一张「学生访客票」。

examples.en: The student guest pass was listed separately in my athletics ticket account.
examples.zh: 「学生访客票」在我的校体育票务账户里单独列出。

words.enDefinition: a pass for eligible students covering multiple events in a season

examples.en: My roommate bought a student season pass because she goes to most games.
examples.zh: 室友买了张「学生赛季通票」，因为大部分比赛她都去看。

examples.en: We checked which sports the student season pass covered before making a decision.
examples.zh: 做决定前，我们查了这张「学生赛季通票」涵盖哪些体育项目。

words.enDefinition: an area at a venue set aside for student spectators

examples.en: I met my classmates in the student section before the match.
examples.zh: 比赛前，我在「学生看台」见到了同学。

examples.en: The student section was on the same level as the team benches.
examples.zh: 「学生看台」和球队替补席在同一层。

words.enDefinition: the number of event tickets set aside for eligible students

examples.en: The student ticket allotment for the opening game ran out before my lecture.
examples.zh: 开场赛的「学生票配额」在我上课前就用完了。

examples.en: The university increased its student ticket allotment for the final day of competition.
examples.zh: 学校增加了最后一个比赛日的「学生票配额」。

words.enDefinition: a ticket offered specifically to people eligible as students

examples.en: I got a student ticket for the match through the university website.
examples.zh: 我通过学校网站拿到了一张比赛的「学生门票」。

examples.en: The venue listed a student ticket alongside the standard adult ticket online.
examples.zh: 场馆在网上把「学生门票」和普通成人票列在一起。

words.enDefinition: a website where eligible students can manage their event tickets

examples.en: The student ticket portal listed both the basketball game and the swim meet.
examples.zh: 「学生票务平台」上既列了篮球赛，也列了游泳比赛。

examples.en: I checked the student ticket portal for the latest date and venue information.
examples.zh: 我在「学生票务平台」上查看了最新的日期和场馆信息。

collocations: list events in the student ticket portal

words.enDefinition: an album made from sessions recorded for release rather than at a live concert

examples.en: We compared the first studio album with the recording from the band's university tour.
examples.zh: 我们把第一张「录音室专辑」和乐队大学巡演的录音作了比较。

examples.en: The artist finished her studio album while working at a café near our campus.
examples.zh: 在我们校园附近的咖啡馆打工期间，那位艺人完成了自己的「录音室专辑」。

words.enDefinition: A secondary story running alongside the main plot.

examples.en: The subplot about the missing notebook was funnier than the main story for me.
examples.zh: 对我来说，丢笔记本的「支线情节」比主线故事还好笑。

examples.en: The film dropped a subplot from the book to spend more time with the family.
examples.zh: 电影删掉了书里的一段「支线情节」，把更多篇幅留给了这一家人。

words.enDefinition: the replacement of one player with another during a game

examples.en: The coach made a substitution a few minutes after the second half started.
examples.zh: 下半场开始几分钟后，教练进行了「换人调整」。

examples.en: We waited for the substitution while the referee confirmed which player was leaving.
examples.zh: 裁判确认哪位队员离场时，我们等着「换人调整」。

words.enDefinition: The language in which the subtitles are displayed.

examples.en: I changed the subtitle language so my visiting cousin could follow what people were saying.
examples.zh: 我换了「字幕语言」，方便来做客的表亲看懂人物在说什么。

examples.en: The menu let us choose the subtitle language while keeping the same audio track.
examples.zh: 菜单允许我们选「字幕语言」，同时保留原先那条音轨。

words.enDefinition: A version presented with written subtitles alongside the spoken dialogue.

examples.en: The cinema showed a subtitled version of the comedy for students in our language class.
examples.zh: 影院给我们语言班的同学放了那部喜剧的「字幕版」。

examples.en: I chose the subtitled version because I liked hearing the actors' voices in the film.
examples.zh: 我喜欢听片中演员本来的声音，就选了「字幕版」。

words.enDefinition: Describes subtitles that appear before or after the matching speech or sound.

examples.en: I noticed the subtitles were out of sync when the characters started talking over dinner.
examples.zh: 角色们刚在晚饭时聊起来，我发现「字幕与音频不同步」。

examples.en: The menu was slow to open, and the subtitles were out of sync again.
examples.zh: 菜单打开得很慢，而且「字幕与音频不同步」的问题又出现了。

collocations: notice the subtitles are out of sync
the subtitles were slightly out of sync
subtitles out of sync with the dialogue

words.enDefinition: An acting part that is less central than the lead but contributes to the story.

examples.en: My favorite actor had a supporting role as the librarian who remembered everyone's name.
examples.zh: 我最喜欢的演员演的是「配角」，那位记得每个人名字的图书管理员。

examples.en: One student thought the actor in a supporting role should have had more scenes.
examples.zh: 有位同学觉得演「配角」的那位演员应该多几场戏。

collocations: cast someone in a supporting role

words.enDefinition: Audio arranged to make sounds seem to come from several directions.

examples.en: The surround sound made it seem as though we were standing beside the river.
examples.zh: 「环绕声」让我们感觉好像就站在那条河边。

examples.en: I noticed the surround sound most during a scene with footsteps coming from behind.
examples.zh: 有一场戏里脚步声从身后传来，那时我最明显地听到了「环绕声」。

words.enDefinition: translated words displayed above a stage during an opera or play

examples.en: I followed the surtitles when I couldn't understand the Italian words.
examples.zh: 听不懂意大利语唱词时，我就跟着看「舞台上方的译文字幕」。

examples.en: The opera used surtitles that we could read from the back row.
examples.zh: 这场歌剧使用了「舞台上方的译文字幕」，坐在最后一排也能看清。

words.enDefinition: to exchange the controllers two players are using

examples.en: We decided to swap controllers between rounds so I could try the smaller one.
examples.zh: 两轮之间，我们决定「互换手柄」，让我试一下小一点的。

examples.en: My roommate asked whether we could swap controllers before the next puzzle.
examples.zh: 室友问下一道谜题开始前能不能「互换手柄」。

words.enDefinition: a performer prepared to cover several ensemble parts as needed

examples.en: The swing performer had learned three of the dancers' parts by opening night.
examples.zh: 到首演之夜，「多角色替补演员」已经学会了三位舞者的戏份。

examples.en: A swing performer took over one ensemble part when a dancer was absent.
examples.zh: 一位舞者缺席时，「多角色替补演员」顶上了一个群舞角色。

words.enDefinition: the small flat implement a player uses to hit a table tennis ball

examples.en: The club lent me a table tennis bat for the lunch break tournament.
examples.zh: 社团借给我一把「乒乓球拍」，参加午休时的小比赛。

examples.en: I borrowed a table tennis bat after leaving mine in the campus locker.
examples.zh: 我把自己的拍子落在校园储物柜里了，就借了一把「乒乓球拍」。

collocations: rubber on a table tennis bat

words.enDefinition: a game played around a table with physical components or spoken rules

examples.en: Our group chose a tabletop game because the common room had no television.
examples.zh: 公共休息室没有电视，我们小组就选了一个「桌面游戏」。

examples.en: I tried a tabletop game that needed only paper, pencils and conversation.
examples.zh: 我试了一个「桌面游戏」，只需要纸、铅笔和交谈。

words.enDefinition: a game where players describe characters' choices in a shared imagined setting

examples.en: I tried a tabletop role-playing game in which we planned a town festival.
examples.zh: 我试了一个「桌面角色扮演游戏」，我们在里面筹办小镇庆典。

examples.en: Our tabletop role-playing game started with everyone describing where their character lived.
examples.zh: 我们的「桌面角色扮演游戏」一开始，大家描述了各自角色住的地方。

words.enDefinition: to bend forward briefly to acknowledge applause after a performance

examples.en: The violinist returned to take a bow beside the two student actors.
examples.zh: 小提琴手回到台上，站在两位学生演员旁「鞠躬致意」。

examples.en: Our director told us to take a bow together at the very end.
examples.zh: 导演让我们在最后一起「鞠躬致意」。

collocations: come out to take a bow
take a bow with the cast
take a bow at the end

words.enDefinition: To stop briefly and rest before continuing an activity.

examples.en: I went to take a breather while my roommate looked for the class schedule.
examples.zh: 室友去找课程时间表时，我去「歇了口气」。

examples.en: We decided to take a breather by the windows after walking around the track.
examples.zh: 绕跑道走完后，我们决定到窗边「歇口气」。

words.enDefinition: to play one more turn before the next person acts

examples.en: The card let me take an extra turn after finishing that set.
examples.zh: 集齐那套牌后，这张牌让我能「多行动一个回合」。

examples.en: My roommate asked why I could take an extra turn that round.
examples.zh: 室友问我为什么那轮能「多行动一个回合」。

collocations: be allowed to take an extra turn
choose to take an extra turn
let someone take an extra turn

words.enDefinition: to undo a play you have already made

examples.en: We agreed beginners could take back a move in the practice round.
examples.zh: 我们约好，在练习轮里新手可以「撤回一步」。

examples.en: My friend asked if I wanted to take back a move after noticing the clue.
examples.zh: 看到线索后，朋友问我想不想「撤回一步」。

collocations: ask to take back a move
be allowed to take back a move
let someone take back a move

words.enDefinition: to go onto the playing field to begin or resume play

examples.en: We watched both teams take the field just as our friends reached the stands.
examples.zh: 朋友们刚到看台，我们就看到两队「进入运动场比赛」。

examples.en: The referee waited for the visiting team to take the field after the break.
examples.zh: 休息结束后，裁判等客队「进入运动场比赛」。

words.enDefinition: tells performers to get into position for a performance or scene

examples.en: The stage manager said "Take your places," and we went quietly to our spots.
examples.zh: 舞台监督说「各就各位」，我们就轻轻走到各自的位置。

examples.en: Take your places behind the curtain before the music for the next scene starts.
examples.zh: 下一场的音乐放起来之前，请在幕布后「各就各位」。

collocations: wait for the signal to take your places

words.enDefinition: A program in which a host talks with guests about their lives or work.

examples.en: I saw the director on a talk show explaining how the film came together.
examples.zh: 我看到导演在一档「访谈节目」里介绍这部电影是怎么拍出来的。

examples.en: The talk show featured a guest who had turned a campus project into a documentary.
examples.zh: 这档「访谈节目」邀请了一位把校园项目拍成纪录片的嘉宾。

collocations: a guest on a talk show

words.enDefinition: to make small rhythmic taps while listening to a piece of music

examples.en: I began to tap along when the band played a tune I knew.
examples.zh: 乐队演奏一首我认识的曲子时，我开始「跟着节奏轻打拍子」。

examples.en: My cousin couldn't help but tap along quietly at the back of the room.
examples.zh: 表亲在屋后忍不住「跟着节奏轻轻打拍子」。

words.enDefinition: a dance style using shoes that produce rhythmic tapping sounds

examples.en: Their tap dance could be heard clearly from the other room.
examples.zh: 在隔壁房间也能听清他们跳「踢踏舞」的声音。

examples.en: My classmate tried tap dance for the first time at an arts workshop.
examples.zh: 同学在一次艺术工作坊里第一次尝试了「踢踏舞」。

words.enDefinition: a shirt worn by members of a sports team when they play

examples.en: I wore my team jersey to class before the last match of the season.
examples.zh: 赛季最后一场比赛前，我穿着「球队球衣」去上课。

examples.en: The captain gave me a clean team jersey after I forgot to bring mine.
examples.zh: 我忘了带球衣，队长给了我一件干净的「球队球衣」。

words.enDefinition: the process of signing up an entire team for an event or league

examples.en: We completed team registration when the last player sent their student identification details.
examples.zh: 最后一名队员发来学生证信息后，我们完成了「团队报名」。

examples.en: The website displayed a separate deadline for team registration and individual signups that term.
examples.zh: 那学期，网站分别显示了「团队报名」和个人报名的截止日期。

words.enDefinition: the official or recorded list of people who are members of a team

examples.en: I checked the team roster before submitting our entries for the campus tournament.
examples.zh: 提交校园比赛报名之前，我核对了「球队名单」。

examples.en: The captain added my roommate to the team roster before the first match.
examples.zh: 第一场比赛前，队长把我室友加进了「球队名单」。

collocations: add a player to the team roster

words.enDefinition: a scarf displaying the colours or emblem of a sports team

examples.en: She waved her team scarf when the players walked out together.
examples.zh: 球员一起出场时，她挥了挥「球队应援围巾」。

examples.en: I borrowed a team scarf because my coat wasn't warm enough.
examples.zh: 我的外套不够暖和，就借了一条「球队应援围巾」。

words.enDefinition: A very brief early preview intended to create interest without revealing much about the story.

examples.en: The teaser trailer showed the location and a few faces without telling us the story.
examples.zh: 「先导预告片」只展示了地点和几张面孔，没告诉我们讲什么故事。

examples.en: Our film club watched the teaser trailer before the longer preview appeared later that month.
examples.zh: 当月晚些时候正式长预告发布前，电影社先看了「先导预告片」。

words.enDefinition: a rehearsal that integrates equipment cues with the performers' actions

examples.en: Our technical rehearsal took longer because we paused to check each lighting change.
examples.zh: 每次灯光变化我们都停下来核对，所以「技术合成排练」时间长了一些。

examples.en: At the technical rehearsal, I heard the scene's new music for the first time.
examples.zh: 「技术合成排练」时，我第一次听到那场戏的新配乐。

words.enDefinition: An informal way to say the next episode becomes available to watch.

examples.en: My roommate asked when the next episode drops so we could arrange to watch it together.
examples.zh: 室友问「下一集什么时候上线」，好约个时间一起看。

examples.en: We decided to leave the discussion until the next episode drops at the weekend.
examples.zh: 我们决定等周末「下一集上线」时再讨论。

collocations: the next episode drops on Friday
ask when the next episode drops
wait until the next episode drops

words.enDefinition: an organisation that puts on stage plays or other theatrical productions

examples.en: The student theatre company chose three short plays for the spring semester.
examples.zh: 学生「剧团」为春季学期选了三部短剧。

examples.en: My classmate joined a theatre company that performs new plays by local writers.
examples.zh: 同学加入了一个「剧团」，演出本地作者创作的新剧。

words.enDefinition: a theatre arrangement where the audience sits around the central stage

examples.en: The school staged the play as theatre in the round, with the audience on all sides.
examples.zh: 学校采用了「环绕式剧场」，观众从各个方向围着表演者坐。

examples.en: I had never seen theatre in the round before our class visited that small venue.
examples.zh: 在全班去那家小场馆前，我从没见过「环绕式剧场」。

collocations: staging for theatre in the round
space designed for theatre in the round

words.enDefinition: the staged presentation of a play or other theatrical work

examples.en: The students chose a small theatre production they could tour to neighbouring campuses.
examples.zh: 同学们选了个小型「剧场演出」，可以到附近的校园巡演。

examples.en: I worked on my first theatre production in the spring of my final year.
examples.zh: 大四春季，我第一次参与了「剧场演出」。

words.enDefinition: a booklet giving information about a production and its performers

examples.en: I checked the theatre programme to see who played the main character.
examples.zh: 我翻了翻「剧场节目册」，看看谁演主角。

examples.en: The theatre programme included two pages about how the students developed the piece.
examples.zh: 「剧场节目册」里有两页介绍同学们是如何创作这部作品的。

words.enDefinition: The release of a film for public showings in movie theaters.

examples.en: We waited for the theatrical release because the film was made for a large screen.
examples.zh: 这部片是为大银幕拍的，所以我们等它「院线上映」。

examples.en: The film society asked whether the documentary would get a theatrical release in our town.
examples.zh: 电影社问这部纪录片会不会在我们镇上「院线上映」。

words.enDefinition: to put thread through the small opening in a needle

examples.en: It took me a moment to thread a needle in the dim room.
examples.zh: 房间光线很暗，我花了一会儿才「给针穿好线」。

examples.en: My roommate asked me to thread a needle before she mended the bag.
examples.zh: 室友补包之前，请我先「给针穿线」。

collocations: thread a needle with cotton thread

words.enDefinition: a basketball shot worth three points when successfully made from outside the three-point line

examples.en: A late three-pointer brought our team within one point just before the final buzzer.
examples.zh: 终场哨前，一个比赛末段的「三分球」把我们和对手的差距缩到一分。

examples.en: My roommate attempted a three-pointer after catching the pass near the side of the court.
examples.zh: 室友在球场一侧接到传球后，尝试投了一个「三分球」。

words.enDefinition: a football restart taken by throwing the ball from the touchline after the whole ball crosses it

examples.en: The referee awarded a throw-in after the ball went past the line beside us.
examples.zh: 球出了我们旁边的边线后，裁判判了「掷界外球」。

examples.en: Our team took a quick throw-in while the others were moving down the pitch.
